sections.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
sections.abstract: The authors count tropical matching fields and hyperplane-sequence types, deriving the same first-order asymptotic for regular triangulations of products of simplices and comparing real and tropical order types.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction identifies the regular-triangulation estimate as answering a question of Santos; the paper also bridges combinatorics, tropical/algebraic geometry, and optimization. Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations at the snapshot, so this placement reflects the explicit result and cross-field scope, not observed uptake.
sections.claimed_result: For each fixed integer r, the authors show the number of regular triangulations of Δ^{n−1}×Δ^{r−1} is n^{(r−1)^2 n+o(n)} as n→∞; the paper also establishes first-order counting comparisons for associated tropical order types.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The stated asymptotics hold with r fixed as n tends to infinity; the objects include coherent matching fields, tropical hyperplane-sequence types, and regular triangulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The fixed-r asymptotic is not a uniform two-parameter estimate when r grows with n; it does not by itself settle algorithmic complexity questions for linear programs or games.

sections.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in 2D Euler Equations
sections.abstract: For stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices, the authors give a sharp integral criterion, based on an envelope of vorticity L^p norms, separating unique from nonunique Euler evolution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors state both directions of a sharp criterion for every finite nondecreasing envelope, rather than only an example or a one-sided sufficient condition. Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations at the snapshot, and searches checked did not surface independent expert discussion; placement is based on the theorem's precise scope and content.
sections.claimed_result: Writing I_Θ=∫_{p₀}^{∞} Θ(p)⁻¹ dp, the authors prove uniqueness for every array in their class when I_Θ diverges, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions; when it converges, they construct an array with two distinct unforced Lagrangian evolutions from the same data.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The dichotomy concerns a specified class of stationary arrays of disjoint, compactly supported neutral vortices and a finite nondecreasing envelope Θ controlling vorticity L^p norms.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly note that this does not settle sharpness of the classical Yudovich criterion for general unbounded vorticities; the result is limited to the stated neutral-array class.

sections.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on Z^d
sections.abstract: For d≥2, the authors give an explicit exponential upper bound on the probability that an n-step self-avoiding walk reaches distance at least vn, yielding a high-probability displacement bound of order n/exp(c log* n).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It makes a previously qualitative sub-ballisticity result quantitative, derives a bridge-partition estimate, and is cross-listed between probability and logic because of its proof-theoretic analysis. Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations at the snapshot; no independent expert discussion was found in searches checked.
sections.claimed_result: The authors bound the probability of linear displacement by exp(−n/T(v)) for an explicit function T and sufficiently large n; they derive displacement at most n/exp(c log* n) with very high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The uniform law on length-n self-avoiding walks starting at the origin in the hypercubic lattice Z^d, for each fixed d≥2.
sections.unique_caveat: The resulting displacement scale is a quantitative improvement, not a sharp asymptotic; the paper says a stronger bound would follow if the normalized bridge partition function had the expected polynomial decay, which is not proved here.

sections.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
sections.abstract: The authors prove global well-posedness near a Maxwellian for the Landau equation in bounded C^3 domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions, covering −3≤γ≤1 including Coulomb interactions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed global strong-solution result spans the full stated interaction range, including Coulomb, and treats two boundary laws in bounded domains. Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations at the snapshot, with no independent expert discussion surfaced by searches checked; ranking rests on the theorem's scope, not measured attention.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Perturbations are small and compatible with a Maxwellian; the spatial domain is bounded with C^3 boundary, and the boundary condition is either in-flow or diffuse reflection.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a near-equilibrium theorem under compatibility and boundary-regularity assumptions, not a large-data global result.

sections.title: Shifted convolutions of divisor functions
sections.abstract: For fixed positive integers k,l and a nonzero fixed shift h, the author proves a power-saving asymptotic for a smooth weighted correlation of the k- and l-fold divisor functions at n and n+h.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction says the all-k,l theorem supplies cases with k,l≥3 not previously known, extending a classical shifted-correlation problem. Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations at the snapshot; a general number-theory paper-list post surfaced, but not independent mathematical analysis, so attention evidence remains slight.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes a main term with singular series S_{k,l}(h)(k−1)!(l−1)! x(log x)^{k+l−2}∫Φ, with a power-saving error, for the weighted sum specified in Theorem 1.1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed integers k,l≥1, fixed nonzero h, a smooth compactly supported weight Φ on (0,∞), and the asymptotic as x→∞.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated theorem does not assert uniformity as h, k, or l vary with x; the result is a preprint claim and its proof has not been independently checked here.
